html:
The Belarusian People's Republic was a state declared in Minsk on 25 March 1918, under German occupation, by the Rada, a council of Belarusian national activists.

It never controlled real territory or an army, and Germany did not recognise it. When German troops left, the Red Army took Minsk and the Bolsheviks set up a Soviet Belarusian republic in 1919. The Rada went into exile, where it still exists, the oldest government in exile in the world. Its white red white flag was adopted again by Belarus in 1991, dropped by Lukashenko in 1995, and carried by the crowds of the 2020 protests. Its founding day, 25 March, is kept as Freedom Day by the opposition.
sum: The Belarusian People's Republic was a state declared in Minsk on 25 March 1918, under German occupation, by the Rada, a council of Belarusian national activists.
